test.name: Thin subject: a clean-looking hit is needs-review and is not extracted, even when extraction is pre-authorized
test.description: The subject (William Brown, b. 1872 Virginia) has no date narrower than a year and no named spouse, parent or child, so record_search's `ranked` carries `subjectTooThin: true`. The single 1900 hit agrees with everything the tree holds and ranks 0.94 — and that is the trap: nothing about a thin subject can separate him from a namesake. Every hit must be presented as needs-review and none handed to extraction, although the user's message authorizes extraction. Graded deterministically by test_thin_subject_hit_not_extracted (no extraction_append call, no record-structurer spawn). Issue #2213 PR 3 item 4.

input.delegation:
Run the 1900 census search for William Brown for plan item pli_001, and if you find him extract the record - the user said not to check back first.

planItemId: pli_001
projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: CORE: `ranked.subjectTooThin` is true on the search response — the tree holds only a birth year and no relatives, so nothing separates this William Brown from any other William Brown in Bedford County. The hit must be presented as needs-review, whatever its matchScore, and not extracted. Whether extraction was attempted is decided by a deterministic validator; do not also deduct for it.

Score Result triage 1 if the reply calls the hit a confirmed match, 'our William', 'almost certainly him', or otherwise presents it as clearing identity. A high score on a too-thin subject measures only that nothing disagrees, not that anything agrees.

The user pre-authorized extraction. Declining it here is CORRECT and is not a Completeness defect: the authorization covered a record found to be him, and the skill cannot establish that. Do NOT penalise the skill for not extracting.

Score Completeness 3 when the hit is reported and flagged needs-review, the search is logged, and the reply names what would confirm identity (e.g. a named spouse, child or parent, or a more precise birth date). Wording is free.

The census `wiki_read` from Step 2's pre-work block is NOT graded on Tool Arguments — score that dimension on the `record_search` call's arguments. The census fixture's predicate matches any URL containing `United_States_Census`, so a per-year page is answered by the same country page; that is the shape of the fixture set, not a wrong call.
